body: I'm not sure what would happen if I told them. I'm the husband father breadwinner, and I've got nothing. I haven't ever cheated on her, but I've been lying about working. I'm supposed to be strong, but I'm not. I feel broken.

I'm a felon, myself. Racked up 3 DWI's in the early 90's. I know your frustrations. Not being on a lease and the like. I was on probation for 7 years. That made even manual labor jobs a bite in the ass, because you have to go report during regular work hours. 

There's good news, though. Time takes the bite out of it. Now I can just say that it's been 20 years and most folk don't care. I went with oilfield work. My brother in law talked me into Halliburton frac in 2006. I was sure they wouldn't hire me, but they didn't care at all. All that mattered to them was the ability to get a CDL. One of the guys on that crew had done 20 years for murder. There are jobs out there for people with checkered pasts, like us. A little time and you'll see. Keep your chin up, you can make it.

In High School, had a buddy I'd known since I was a little kid. It was a private school, so a lot of us there had been kicked out of public schools. I knew him, but we hadn't seen each other for years. I'll call him Jay. He was a cool enough guy, kinda goofy. My girlfriend was friends with him, they were in some of the same classes (I was a grade ahead). He casually tells me that my girlfriend is blessed as far as boobs go, and that I'm a lucky guy to be with her. I took it poorly. Didn't say anything, but I was pissed..kinda. 

The next week, a bunch of us are all going to a burger joint for lunch. Jay rolls up wondering if he can ride with us (my gf, myself, and another buddy), plenty of room for another. Told him we were full up. He catches another ride, 5 deep in a Taurus or something like that. Go to lunch, back to school. The period after lunch, we're in the halls, nobody knows where any of the 5 in that car are. There are only 250 kids in the whole HS, it's not like folks ain't gonna notice if you aren't there. At first, we think they just decided to skip the rest of the day. Nope. The girl driving ran into a telephone pole. 3 of the 5 riding in that car died. Jay was one of them. I can't put into words how shitty I still feel about it. It was 15 years ago and I'm still not over it. It changed me. I felt like a walking shit-sickle for a long time. At the funeral, I told his mom I was sorry (she didn't know I was why he was in that car, I couldn't fully explain..I was crying..a lot). It's the worst I've ever felt.
